title: Acid Warehouse, from a kick to a track
description: The core capstone built the way a producer builds it: one lesson at a time, from a kick to an arranged, mixed track.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Acid Warehouse
tracks.blurb: Every lesson starts from the code you finished in the one before; the last is the whole track.

lessons.title: The pulse
lessons.goal: Start the track: a 909 kick on every beat and open hats on the offbeats, at 126 BPM.
lessons.concept:
This line of lessons builds one track, **Acid Warehouse**, the way a producer does: a loop that grows, then gets shaped. Each lesson starts from the code you finished in the one before.

It starts with the pulse. **Four on the floor** (a kick on every beat) is the heartbeat of house and techno, and an **open hat on every offbeat** gives it the push. 126 BPM is a touch faster than house; it suits acid.
lessons.starter:
// Acid Warehouse
setcpm(126/4)            // BPM ÷ 4 beats: 1 cycle = 1 bar

tasks.text: Add a part called kick: a TR-909 kick on every beat, and play it.
tasks.hint: const kick = s("bd*4").bank("RolandTR909"), then stack(kick).

tasks.text: Add a part called hats: an open hat on every offbeat, at gain .55.
tasks.hint: const hats = s("[~ oh]*4").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.55), then stack(kick, hats).

summary: A kick on every beat and an open hat on every offbeat: the pulse.
Every lesson in this line starts where the last one ended.

lessons.title: Clap and ticks
lessons.goal: Add the clap on 2 and 4 and swung 16th hats.
lessons.concept:
The **clap** on beats 2 and 4 is the backbeat; a little **reverb** (`.room`) sets it back, and it gets its own **orbit** so that reverb is the clap’s alone.

**Ticks** are closed hats on every 16th. A gain pattern puts the weight on the beat, and **swing** (`.swingBy(.16, 8)`, about 58%) delays every second 16th so the grid stops feeling like a machine.

tasks.text: Add a part called clap on beats 2 and 4, with a little room on orbit 2.
tasks.hint: const clap = s("~ cp ~ cp").bank("RolandTR909").room(.2).orbit(2), and stack it.

tasks.text: Add a part called ticks: closed hats on all 16 sixteenths with a gain pattern.
tasks.hint: const ticks = s("hh*16").bank("RolandTR909").gain("[.4 .2 .3 .2]*4"), and stack it.

tasks.text: Swing the ticks: .16 over 8ths, about 58%.
tasks.hint: .swingBy(.16, 8) on the ticks line.

summary: Clap on 2 and 4, in its own room on its own orbit.
16th ticks with a gain pattern and .swingBy(.16, 8).

lessons.title: The bass
lessons.goal: Add an offbeat bass in C minor, short and dark.
lessons.concept:
One `const key` keeps every pitched part in tune; the bass reads it with `.scale(key)`. Scale degree 0 is the root (C), −2 is two steps down (A♭), so the line leans and comes home.

The bass plays on the **offbeats**, between the kicks, so the two never fight for the low end. A short **decay**, no **sustain** and a closed **low-pass** keep it a thump rather than a drone. It sits on **orbit 4**, which the kick will duck later.

tasks.text: Add const key = "C:minor" and a part called bass: scale degrees [~ 0] [~ 0] [~ 0] [~ -2] on a sawtooth, octave 2, on orbit 4.
tasks.hint: const key = "C:minor" at the top, then const bass = n("[~ 0] [~ 0] [~ 0] [~ -2]").scale(key).s("sawtooth").octave(2).gain(.7).orbit(4), and stack it.

tasks.text: Make it short and dark: low-pass 450 Hz, decay .15, no sustain.
tasks.hint: .lpf(450).decay(.15).sustain(0) on the bass line.

summary: const key + .scale(key) keeps parts in tune.
An offbeat bass never fights the kick.
Short decay, no sustain, closed filter: a thump.

lessons.title: The 303 line
lessons.goal: Add the acid line: sixteen steps through a ladder filter.
lessons.concept:
The acid voice is a **TB-303**: a sawtooth, a 16-step line that mostly sits on the root with octave jumps, and a **ladder filter** with high **resonance** and a fast **filter envelope** (`.lpenv`, `.lpdecay`), so every note goes "wow".

`.ftype("ladder")` picks the 303-style filter; `.lpq(18)` is the resonance; `.lpdecay(.15)` is how fast the envelope closes. The acid gets **orbit 5**, its own space.

tasks.text: Add a part called acid: a 16-step sawtooth line on orbit 5.
tasks.hint: const acid = note("[c2 c2 c3 c2] [eb2 c2 c3 g1] [c2 ~ bb2 c2] [c3 c2 eb2 g2]").s("sawtooth").decay(.2).sustain(0).gain(.55).orbit(5), and stack it.

tasks.text: Give it the 303 filter: ladder, cutoff 900, resonance 18, a fast filter decay.
tasks.hint: .ftype("ladder").lpf(900).lpq(18).lpdecay(.15) on the acid line.

summary: A 303 line: 16 steps, mostly the root, octave jumps.
Ladder filter + high resonance + a fast filter decay.

lessons.title: Accents
lessons.goal: Accent some steps: louder and brighter on the same notes.
lessons.concept:
On a 303 an **accented** step is louder *and* its filter opens further. Strudel has no accent button, so we build it from two patterns that line up step by step: `.velocity` for loudness and `.lpenv` for filter depth.

Accent three or four steps per bar, never all of them: the contrast is the point.

tasks.text: Add a velocity pattern with four accented steps (1) and the rest at .6.
Open the filter more on the same steps with an lpenv pattern.

summary: An accent = louder (.velocity) + brighter (.lpenv) on the same steps.

lessons.title: The sweep
lessons.goal: Open the acid filter slowly over 32 bars, and move the resonance.
lessons.concept:
The magic of acid is the **slow sweep**: the cutoff creeping up over half a minute while the line repeats, until it screams. `saw.range(300, 3000).slow(32)` rises from 300 to 3000 Hz across 32 bars, then falls back.

Sweep the **resonance** on a different clock, a 16-bar sine between 15 and 22, so the sound keeps changing character. Inside an arrangement each section restarts the sweep from its first bar.

tasks.text: Replace the fixed cutoff with a 32-bar saw sweep from 300 to 3000 Hz.
tasks.hint: Change .lpf(900) to .lpf(saw.range(300, 3000).slow(32)) on the acid line.

tasks.text: Move the resonance on a 16-bar sine between 15 and 22.
tasks.hint: Change .lpq(18) to .lpq(sine.range(15, 22).slow(16)).

summary: saw.range(a, b).slow(32): a rise over 32 bars.
Move resonance on a different cycle for variety.

lessons.title: The stab
lessons.goal: Add a two-chord stab and send it through a dub delay modifier.
lessons.concept:
A **stab** is a short chord hit: `chord("<Cm7 Fm7>").voicing()` picks the notes (one chord per bar), `.struct("[~ x]*2")` puts it on the offbeats of 2 and 4.

A **modifier** is a function that takes a part and returns it changed: `const dubDelay = x => x.delay(.4).delaysync(3/16).delayfeedback(.55).orbit(3)`. Apply it where the part is played, `dubDelay(stab)`, so the stab itself stays clean and the same delay can go on anything later.

tasks.text: Add a part called stab: a Cm7 / Fm7 chord stab on the offbeats of 2 and 4, filtered at 1400 Hz.
tasks.hint: const stab = chord("<Cm7 Fm7>").voicing().struct("[~ x]*2").s("sawtooth").lpf(1400).decay(.15).sustain(0).gain(.45), and stack it.

tasks.text: Write a modifier called dubDelay (a dotted-eighth delay on orbit 3) and play the stab through it.
tasks.hint: const dubDelay = x => x.delay(.4).delaysync(3/16).delayfeedback(.55).orbit(3), then dubDelay(stab) in the stack.

summary: chord(…).voicing().struct(…): which notes, and when.
A modifier is a function you apply where a part is played.

lessons.title: Sections
lessons.goal: Name intro, drop and outro, then arrange them.
lessons.concept:
A track is sections in a row. A **section** is a stack with a name: the **intro** is drums only, so a DJ can mix in; the **drop** is everything; the **outro** is drums again.

`arrange([16, intro], [32, drop], [16, outro])` plays them for that many bars each. Changes land on **16-bar phrases**, where dancers expect them.

tasks.text: Define three sections: intro (kick, hats, ticks), drop (everything, with dubDelay(stab)), outro (kick, hats). Play drop for now.
tasks.hint: const intro = stack(kick, hats, ticks), const drop = stack(kick, clap, hats, ticks, bass, acid, dubDelay(stab)), const outro = stack(kick, hats); end the file with drop.

tasks.text: Arrange them: 16 bars of intro, 32 of drop, 16 of outro.
tasks.hint: Replace the last line with arrange([16, intro], [32, drop], [16, outro]).

summary: Sections are named stacks; arrange() plays them for so many bars each.
Drums-only intro and outro for the DJ.

lessons.title: Riser and breakdown
lessons.goal: Add a build with a noise riser, and a breakdown without the kick.
lessons.concept:
**Tension and release.** A **build** section adds a **riser**: pink noise whose high-pass sweeps up over 16 bars (`.hpf(saw.range(200, 6000).slow(16))`), so the sound thins and climbs into the drop.

A **breakdown** takes the kick away for 8 bars and leaves the acid and the stab hanging in their echoes. When the kick returns, the room lifts.

tasks.text: Add a part called riser (pink noise, high-pass sweeping 200 to 6000 Hz over 16 bars) and a 16-bar build section between the intro and the drop.
tasks.hint: const riser = s("pink*16").hpf(saw.range(200, 6000).slow(16)).gain(.2); const build = stack(kick, hats, ticks, bass, riser); arrange([16, intro], [16, build], [32, drop], [16, outro]).

tasks.text: Add an 8-bar breakdown after the drop: hats, acid and the stab, no kick.
tasks.hint: const breakdown = stack(hats, acid, dubDelay(stab)), then arrange([16, intro], [16, build], [32, drop], [8, breakdown], [16, outro]).

summary: A riser is noise with a rising high-pass.
A breakdown drops the kick; the return is the release.

lessons.title: Project: The mix
lessons.goal: Carve the parts apart, duck the bass under the kick, and finish the arrangement.
lessons.concept:
Mixing in Strudel is three tools. **High-pass** everything that isn’t bass, so the low end belongs to the kick and the bass. **Duck** the bass under the kick with a `pump` modifier (`duckorbit(4)` points at the bass’s orbit), applied only in sections where the bass plays, because ducking a silent orbit is an error (gap G14).

Then the full shape: intro, build, drop, breakdown, a second drop, outro. 104 bars at 126 BPM is about three and a half minutes.

tasks.text: High-pass the clap and stab at 200 Hz, the hats at 300, the ticks at 400.
tasks.hint: .hpf(200) on clap and stab, .hpf(300) on hats, .hpf(400) on ticks.

tasks.text: Write a pump modifier that ducks orbit 4 and apply it to the kick in build and drop only.
tasks.hint: const pump = x => x.duckorbit(4).duckdepth(.7); then pump(kick) in build and drop, plain kick in intro and outro.

tasks.text: Finish the arrangement: bring the drop back for 16 bars after the breakdown, before the outro.
tasks.hint: arrange([16, intro], [16, build], [32, drop], [8, breakdown], [16, drop], [16, outro]).

summary: High-pass what isn’t bass.
Duck the bass only where it plays.
Intro, build, drop, breakdown, drop, outro: a track.
